entities.name: Elisedd ap Gwylog
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Elisedd ap Gwylog, king of Powys in eastern Wales, played a pivotal role in shaping the medieval Welsh identity from 733 to 755 CE. He was the son of Gwylog ap Beli and expanded Powys' territories through strategic alliances and military conquests. 

His reign was marked by the Battle of Hingston Down in 735 CE, where he defeated the forces of Rhodri ap Iago, king of Seisyllwg, and secured the border with the kingdom of Seisyllwg. 

Elisedd ap Gwylog's legacy can be seen in the continued Welsh cultural heritage and the preservation of the Welsh language and traditions. He is remembered as a fierce defender of Welsh independence and a unifying figure for the Welsh people.

"We will not be conquered, we will not be defeated! Our ancestors' blood runs through our veins, and our language will not be silenced." - Elisedd ap Gwylog, quoted in the Annals of Wales.
